faq.q: Which languages and input types does it handle?
faq.a: It recognises many scripts via Tesseract.js, including English, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Urdu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Assamese, Sanskrit and Nepali, plus combined packs like English+Hindi. You can feed it multiple images at once or a single PDF (pages are rendered via pdf.js). Language data of roughly 1–15 MB downloads once per language on first use, then runs offline.

faq.q: How can I improve accuracy on a poor scan?
faq.a: Open Image pre-processing to rotate, scale up (1x–3x; 2x helps small text), adjust contrast, brightness, a black/white threshold, grayscale, sharpen or invert for light-on-dark text. Five presets configure these automatically: Scanned document, Photo of a page, Handwritten notes, Screenshot, and Faded/low contrast. A preview shows exactly what the engine will read, and you can drag to select just one region.

faq.q: Can I control how the output text is laid out?
faq.a: Yes. Page-type (Tesseract PSM) options include Auto mixed page, uniform block, columns, sparse text, single line and single character. The Output setting gives Plain text, Keep line breaks, or Merge into paragraphs. There's also a "Tidy up text" cleaner that rejoins hyphen-split words, normalises quotes and fixes spacing before punctuation.

faq.q: What can I export, and is there a confidence score?
faq.a: After recognition you get an estimated accuracy percentage (coloured green/amber/pink) plus word, character and line counts; it reports 0% and "no text found" rather than a misleading figure when nothing is read. If a tab-like layout is detected it shows a reconstructed table. You can copy the editable text or download it as .txt, .doc or .csv. All processing stays in your browser.
